C-PLATFORM-DURABLE-PACKAGE-ACTIVATION-20.Summary: Replace model-only upgrade state with a production-backed immutable package catalog and crash-safe activation of one code, state, policy, and authority generation, including quarantine, LastKnownGood rollback, and independent recovery boot.
C-PLATFORM-DURABLE-PACKAGE-ACTIVATION-20.Problem: The current upgrade, quarantine, safe-mode, and bisect types are useful models but do not form a durable loader that selects executable package bytes and matching state after a fresh process start. Without one atomic generation pointer, AI-generated updates can leave code, state, policy, and authority out of sync or make recovery depend on the broken optional feature.

Goals.Goal: Store immutable package revisions identified by digest and provenance separately from installation and runtime identities.
Implement stage, compatibility check, migration-on-copy, validation, atomic generation selection, observation, quarantine, and rollback.
Bind every activation to a monotonic epoch consumed by effect fences and runtime handles.
Start LastKnownGood and protected recovery composition without loading optional feature code.
Run core and engine updates through a separately trusted updater with authenticated immutable artifacts and a rollback candidate.
Preserve installation-owned data across compatible disable, rollback, and engine or core updates.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.
C-VNEXT-ARCHITECTURE-DECISION-20260906 and C-KERNEL-EFFECT-FENCE-REVOCATION-20260906 must be applied before this change is planned.
Installing package bytes must never activate code or grant authority.
Package revisions are immutable; in-place overwrite of active executable or state is forbidden.
Migration runs on a copy and rollback selects a prior compatible generation; reverse migration of the only state copy is forbidden.
Exactly one durable Current generation may be visible after recovery.
Recovery, updater, and safe-mode launch paths cannot execute optional user features to become operational.
Ordinary features cannot invoke, reconfigure, impersonate, or supply trust roots to the system updater.
Core and engine candidates require authenticated update metadata, artifact digest verification, compatibility validation, and an independently bootable fallback before selection.
Event delivery is not the source of truth for active package selection.
Incomplete external effects are reconciled, never blindly retried.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Public release publishing, marketplace distribution, or organization-wide key-management operations.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A durable catalog stores immutable package revision, artifact digest, manifest version, dependencies, provenance, requested permissions, compatibility metadata, and install state without executing the package.
A durable generation record binds exact code revision, state generation, policy generation, granted capability set, activation epoch, and prior LastKnownGood pointer.
Activation follows stage, migrate-copy, validate, atomic-select, start, observe, and promote without overwriting the previous generation.
Failpoint and fresh-process tests at every durable transition recover to exactly one admissible Current generation or to protected recovery mode.
An old runtime and its handles cannot regain authority after a newer activation epoch is selected or rolled back.
Health failure during observation quarantines only the candidate revision and restores LastKnownGood without deleting installation data.
Safe mode and recovery launcher start from mandatory trusted composition when optional feature manifests, state, or code are corrupt.
A distinct trusted updater principal is the only authority permitted to stage core or engine candidates and cannot be invoked or reconfigured by an ordinary feature.
Core and engine update tests reject unauthenticated metadata, digest mismatch, wrong platform, incompatible feature ABI, rollback-incompatible state, and missing fallback before switch.
Compatibility negotiation independently covers manifest schema, feature ABI, capability contracts, state schema, host version, and engine profile.
Engine or core update can disable an incompatible optional feature while preserving its immutable package and user data for later recovery.
Operational telemetry records revision, phase, outcome, epoch, timing, and failure class without raw user payload or secrets.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh-process failpoint evidence proves one atomic active generation, LastKnownGood rollback, quarantine, protected recovery boot, stale-epoch denial, preserved data, and truthful Incomplete outcomes.

Assumptions.Assumption: Current SQLite transactional and migration-on-copy primitives can own the generation pointer without turning the event journal into package state.
Executable artifacts can be addressed and verified by immutable digest before a runtime is created.
Existing upgrade models can be adapted or replaced without treating their current tests as production loader evidence.
